block.description: Generate JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) directly inside Terraform/OpenTofu configuration. The provider has no configuration: declare it and use the jwt_signed_token or jwt_hashed_token resources, or the jwt_decoded_token data source.

algorithm.description: HMAC algorithm. One of `HS256`, `HS384`, `HS512`. Defaults to `HS512`.

claims_json.description: The token's claims, as a JSON object.

id.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the signed token. Stable for a given (algorithm, secret, secret_encoding, claims_json) tuple.

kid.description: Optional `kid` (key ID) value to set in the JWT header so downstream verifiers can pick the matching shared secret from a key registry.

secret.description: HMAC secret used to sign the JWT.

secret_encoding.description: How `secret` is encoded. One of `raw`, `base64`, `hex`. Defaults to `raw`.

token.description: The signed JWT, as a compact-serialized string.

block.description: Generates a JWT signed with an HMAC secret (HS256/HS384/HS512). The token is computed locally during apply and stored in state as a sensitive computed attribute.

claims_json.description: The token's claims, as a JSON object.

id.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the signed token. Stable for a given (algorithm, key, claims_json) tuple.

key.description: PEM-encoded RSA or ECDSA private key matching `algorithm`.

kid.description: Optional `kid` (key ID) value to set in the JWT header. Required when consumers look up the public key from a JWKS keyed by `kid` (for example, Google service account JWKS at `https://www.googleapis.com/service_accounts/v1/jwk/<email>`).

token.description: The signed JWT, as a compact-serialized string.

block.description: Generates a JWT signed with an asymmetric private key (RSA or ECDSA). The token is computed locally during apply and stored in state as a sensitive computed attribute.

algorithm.description: Signing algorithm declared in the header `alg` claim.

block.description: Decodes a compact-serialized JWT into its header, claims, and signature. The signature is **not** verified: use this data source to read claims out of a token whose trust is already established by other means (TLS, mTLS, key-rotated upstream service).
